summary: Watchers 5B.1 done. m4: the character slot merge is gone: ModelKit.MergeSlots, MergeCharacterSlots, the merged-mesh tables, SourceMeshOf, IsMerged and SlotGroups, the merged branch of SourceSlots, Inhabitant.MergedSlots, Tuning.CharacterSlotMerge (it sat in the M5B watchers block), the EditMode test Merged_slots_are_the_distinct_colours_and_details_of_each_character, and the PlayMode merged-slots test. Step22c already had the unmerged assertions (AreSame on the catalog mesh), so ProbeTestsM42Look.cs is unchanged. The draw-call budgets still hold: Step22c and Step39h_ pass on every manifest level, and the new Step37x_ logs 39 character slots and 60 of 120 draw calls on the people fixture. m11: the second Step37w_ test is now Step37x_CharacterSlotsAreTheCatalogSlotsWithinTheBudget. Its old body tested the merge, which is removed, so the old name would have been false. It now asserts that every character draws the catalog prefab's own mesh with exactly the prefab's slots, that the clothes alone take the tint, and that the level's draw calls stay within budget. m5 and m41: rewrote the LoadView header (LevelBuilder.ApplyLoad creates the view, GameState.StepLoad drives SetTilt) and the MotionProfile rock comment (GameState.StepRock, then BeginExternalAction of RockTime or RockCarefulTime). Deleted RobotPath.ArcAt, which had no caller. Moved the Robot pulse range to Tuning.RobotLightPulseMin and Max, and the VisionConeView literals to Tuning.ConeClearMargin and Tuning.ConeDrapeReach, all in a new 'M5 5B.1 watchers' block at the end of Tuning.cs. m15 robot: the root transform keeps the rule pose exactly. A new Robot.Body child holds the shell, bumper and light. In LateUpdate the body is interpolated between the poses of the last two fixed steps and turns at most Tuning.RobotTurnRate (540 deg/s), so a reversal is a one-third-second spin. A jump past Tuning.RobotSnapDistance (0.5 m) snaps the body. Step42w_ now covers this with a per-frame turn cap check during a driven reversal. m15 clue: on a split level, LoadView.SpawnClue lays the clue in FurnitureController.RampFrame's frame, so it lies on the slope. If its spread would cross a platform edge or a ramp foot or head, the clue moves (within Tuning.ClueSearchRadius, never through a ChairBlockerMask collider) to the nearest spot where it lies whole on one surface. It stays on the platform it fell on. Flat levels are unchanged. The new Step44x_ checks the platform edge, the floor beside the platform and the ramp on the floor fixture. Results: PlayMode 'Step37|Step38|Step22|Step39h|Step42|Step44' gave 45 of 46. The one failure is Step37e_ ('watchful: the decoy rings are not the seer's tolerance', expected 0.5, got 0.75). That is m14 work in progress in GhostView and GameState, which other agents own, not a watchers file. EditMode ModelM5Tests: 12 of 12. Both new mutants were verified killed under the Unity lock, and the files were restored byte for byte.
